item.title: Senior Advocacy Officer
item.description: We are seeking an exceptional advocate with a policy, legal or related digital rights campaigning background to work with us furthering privacy and civil liberties in the UK at one of the UK’s leading rights NGOs. Initially, this role will be principally challenging facial recognition surveillance and scrutinising police surveillance/AI powers. The Senior Advocacy Officer will help us to lobby UK Parliament to further privacy and wider rights at a critical time – when a legal framework on police use of facial recognition is very soon to be introduced, and police are expanding their use of AI and new surveillance technologies. You’ll build on your strong experience to be a credible and proactive lobbyist in Parliament, write expert briefings and be confident meeting parliamentarians, take a leading role liaising with policy stakeholders, be a leading advocate in the press and the public forum, develop policy positions on key issues, and help drive our public campaigns for change. Senior Advocacy Officer job description Policy Produce policy analysis, research, briefings and reports for dissemination Develop strategic policy recommendations informed by expertise Identify and explore new and emerging policy issues in our key work areas Communicate complex policy issues to varied audiences, whether Parliament, the press or the public Build strong relationships with parliamentarians and advisors across all parties Identify opportunities to further our strategic aims in Parliament, through committees, parliamentary questions and other activities; as well as regional assemblies and on occasion local government Work with stakeholders and pursue collaborative campaigns/coalitions on key issues Develop Big Brother Watch’s relationships with allies across Government, legislative bodies, international organisations, and NGOs Draft formal correspondence, blog posts, presentations, and other documents articulating Big Brother Watch’s policy positions Advocacy Identify campaigns and advocacy opportunities, and feed into campaign plans and materials Write articles and give quotes to press Give pre-recorded and live interviews for TV and radio Uphold Big Brother Watch’s reputational excellence in public fora Help manage media enquiries (our 24/7 media phone is handled on a staff rota system) Closing Date : 21 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Start date - ASAP Application Details First, please read the Job Information Pack. This has full details on how to apply: https://bigbrotherwatch.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Senior-Advocacy-Officer-Job-Information-Pack-July-2026.pdf Please send: • Your CV • A covering letter detailing how you meet the job specification, noting your experience lobbying UK parliament, successful campaign experience, and any experience working on facial recognition/police surveillance technologies. Please tell us why you want to work with Big Brother Watch in particular. (1 page max) To recruitment@bigbrotherwatch.org.uk Website : https://bigbrotherwatch.org.uk

item.title: Constituency Assistant
item.description: Steff Aquarone, MP for North Norfolk, is seeking an organised, thoughtful and dependable Constituency Assistant to join his team permanently in North Walsham. This varied role combines responsibility for the MP’s diary and correspondence with practical support for constituent casework. The successful candidate will help ensure Steff’s time is well managed, commitments are properly planned and everyone contacting the office receives a prompt, compassionate and professional response. One moment may involve arranging meetings, visits or travel; the next may involve supporting a distressed resident, drafting a reply, logging a case or escalating an urgent enquiry. Key responsibilities: • Manage Steff’s diary, meetings, visits, travel and accommodation. • Prepare information and practical details for engagements. • Provide confidential administrative support and assist with surgeries and public events. • Oversee correspondence channels, including the MP inbox. • Triage enquiries and identify urgent, sensitive or safeguarding matters. • Respond clearly and compassionately by email, telephone and in person. • Log cases, gather information and monitor actions and deadlines. • Support the casework team while maintaining confidentiality and data protection. • Occasionally work outside normal hours or travel when required. The ideal candidate will be organised, reliable and attentive to detail. They will remain calm when priorities change, communicate clearly, exercise sound judgement and treat people with patience and dignity. They should be confident using email, digital calendars, case-management systems and shared documents, and able to identify what requires routine handling, specialist casework or Steff’s attention. Previous parliamentary experience is not essential. Relevant experience may come from public services, customer service, executive support or another demanding public-facing environment. Steff’s team is committed to compassion, integrity and high-quality public service. Applications are welcomed from all backgrounds, and reasonable adjustments will be made throughout recruitment and employment. The salary is £26,039 per annum, in accordance with IPSA guidelines. Appointment is subject to the Baseline Personnel Security Standard. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 14 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Closing time: 11.59pm First-round interviews: 26th August in North Walsham Second-round interviews: late August/early September Preferred start date: 1 October 2026 , subject to notice periods and security checks. We will not appoint before the closing date. Application Details Please email your CV and a covering letter of no more than 500 words to tom.garrod@parliament.uk , using the subject line “Constituency Assistant – [Your name]”. Please include examples of managing competing priorities and communicating sensitively with someone in difficult circumstances. Audio or video applications are welcome where this would remove an accessibility barrier. Applicants selected for interview will be contacted on 19 August 2026. We may not be able to contact unsuccessful applicants individually. Website : http://steffanaquarone.com/

item.title: Operations Manager
item.description: We are seeking an experienced, highly organised and proactive Operations Manager to play a central role in keeping our London office running smoothly and supporting our wider team and organisation. The ideal candidate will have strong liberal instincts and support our mission to defend civil liberties in the UK. This is a varied and hands-on role with responsibility across multiple operational areas, ensuring everything runs smoothly behind the scenes. It is a new role to the organisation, initially offered as a 12 month fixed term contract, with the possibility of extension. Flexible working that works for you 16 hours per work, with flexibility as to how these are worked We’re open to a range of working patterns (e.g. school hours, shorter days across the week, or compressed hours, potentially variations across term times / school holidays) Hybrid working, in practice will likely require min. 50% office attendance The rest of our team works full time in-office. However, for this particular part-time role we aim to agree on a working pattern that provides consistency and predictability while fitting around your other commitments. We particularly welcome applications from experienced candidates returning to work after a career break, including parents and carers. Operations Manager job description • Take ownership of the day-to-day running of the London office, ensuring it is organised and efficient • Help co-ordinate logistics for meetings and staff travel • Co-ordinate IT support, equipment and asset management • Lead IT migration projects (e.g. changing software/support suppliers, as directed) • Ensure the office and kitchen are adequately supplied • Support with HR admin including recruitment of staff, volunteers and contractors • Organise staff socials • Organise cycle to work scheme • Liaise with accountants, support basic book-keeping (receipt filing) • Support with internal file storage, physical and digital • Support with maintenance of databases • Assist with postage and physical mailouts to our supporters • Commit to highest standards of data protection • Periodically undertake required office risk assessments Closing Date : 21 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates ASAP Application Details First you must read the Job Information Pack on our website: https://bigbrotherwatch.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Operations-Manager-Job-Information-Pack-July-2026.pdf Then please send: • Your CV • A covering letter detailing how you meet the job specification, your relevant experience and why you want to work with Big Brother Watch in particular. item.title: Caseworker
item.description: Uma Kumaran MP is recruiting a fixed term Caseworker to join her small and busy team. The role will include providing information, advice and support to constituents in Stratford and Bow on a variety of issues and liaising with both local councils, Government agencies, the voluntary sector and others to help resolve matters on behalf of constituents. Key responsibilities: Deal with large numbers of standard queries, as well as assisting on more complex cases from members of the public by phone, email, social media, or face-to-face. Ongoing communication may be required. Log all cases; monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken. Gather relevant information to assist with resolving cases. Draft responses to constituents. Assist surgeries and other meetings and follow up as appropriate. Ensure all enquiries are dealt with in a timely manner. Critically analyse patterns of enquiries and articulate the findings in reports and communication with the MP and other staff members. Manage and monitor casework enquiries received by social media. Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially in line with the data protection legislation. There may be a requirement for the role holder to work outside of the normal working hours and travel for work occasionally. Personal specification: Previous experience of handling casework, either in an MP’s Office, the Civil Service, or a third sector organisation such as the CAB is desirable. Excellent verbal and written communication skills and confidence in interacting with people at all levels and in a variety of circumstances. A compassionate person with a strong sense of justice, a natural ability to empathise with others, and a determination to fight for fair outcomes. Ability to adapt and work effectively as part of a small team who manage diverse and varying workloads collaboratively. Ability to carry out tasks quickly and to a high standard. Being a self-starter with a demonstrable record of taking initiative. Ability to manage a large and varied caseload under pressure. An understanding of the values and aims of our team and the Member of Parliament. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . item.description: Do you have political or local government experience? Are you confident dealing with the press, managing social media outlets and providing political advice to senior local politicians? Are you a member of the Reform Party or do you share the party's beliefs and values? Providing research, political advice and support to the Reform Group Leader and Reform councillors in Hull, you will draft and present reports, provide high quality support, plan agendas, attend and minute meetings and liaise with outside bodies and the press on behalf of the Reform Group. You will assist the group in its relationship with the local press and proactively ensure that the group's messages are developed and communicated widely, through a variety of media outlets. At the same time, you will ensure that key decisions from Group meetings are swiftly implemented and proactively identify issues of political interest, whilst supporting councillors with public speaking engagements and formal council questions and motions. You will be knowledgeable about the functions of a local authority and will be familiar with the roles of councillors and political party groups and will be able to work in a politically sensitive environment. Equally importantly, you will bring considerable initiative to support the Reform Group to undertake their role, and will display a very organised and self-motivated approach, backed by a high level of IT literacy and a sensitive approach to managing confidential information. Finally, you will need to be able to understand the diverse needs of the Reform Group and balance individual councillors' demands and expectations. As well as taking direction from the Leader of the Group you will work closely with the Group Whip and Democratic and Member Support colleagues. item.description: Chris Curtis MP is looking to recruit an organised and highly motivated Office Manger to join his team. This is an excellent opportunity to join the office of an active constituency MP as Office Manager. The successful candidate will lead the administrative operation of a busy Parliamentary office, overseeing the office team, managing the budget and liaising with IPSA on financial and contractual matters. The successful candidate will have strong organisational and people-management skills, sound judgement, and the ability to manage a varied workload, including delegated signoff on relevant areas of office business, in a fast-paced environment. Key Responsibilities Collate all required information from team members to present to MP. Deal with security matters, keep abreast of security guidance, maintain the security system, liaise with external bodies as appropriate. Ensure the office is fully equipped. Have final signoff on all relevant delegated areas from the MP, for example constituent correspondence. Horizon-scanning, anticipate what advice or action may be required; proactively identify problems and resolve them. Identify training opportunities and ensure the office team maintain and develop knowledge of relevant legislation where appropriate. Lead and maintain a highly professional administrative support function for the MP’s office. Liaise with groups/personnel including at Westminster, within the constituency and the general public on the MP’s behalf as necessary. Manage the office team, ensuring accurate personnel records are kept and notifying IPSA of contractual changes as necessary. item.title: PhD Studentship: Masters plus PHD- Sustainability Life Sciences
item.description: Scholarship Opportunity This is an opportunity to undertake a fully funded masters’ degree and an interdisciplinary PhD under the ‘Sustainable Transitions – Leverhulme Doctoral Training Programme’ at the University of Essex. (All tuition fees are covered and an annual stipend provided throughout the Masters and PhD phases.) The purpose of this programme is to train the next generation of interdisciplinary scholars with the skills and expertise to contribute to ‘sustainable transitions’ at local, national and international levels. Applicants with an undergraduate degree in the life sciences or a related subject are invited to put forward a proposal for a PhD research project in the field of environment and sustainability as it relates to the life sciences. The successful applicant will then undertake the following masters’ degrees commencing in January 2027 and further develop their research proposal before proceeding to the PhD phase: MSc Biotechnology Research Proposal You are invited to submit a 1000 word (max) project area proposal that describes the area that you wish to research. This call for proposals is broadly defined, leaving scope for the applicant to develop their own specific research proposal as part of the application. The successful candidate will further develop their proposal in close consultation with the supervisory team during the masters’ year and further during the PhD phase. In your proposal you should identify ONE of the following four disciplines that you would like to integrate into your research to ensure that it your research is interdisciplinary in nature: Law, Government/Political Science, Business, or Sociology. It is not necessary to have any prior knowledge of this additional discipline as you will be given training when you commence your PhD. Training and Support You will receive a range of training and opportunities in the Masters’ phase of the programme. When you commence the PhD phase you will receive support through the Sustainable Transitions training programme, which offers interdisciplinary research methods, secondary discipline training, and ongoing development. Doctoral scholars also have access to £2,500 through Proficio for training courses and £10,000 for research and additional training. You may audit relevant courses and will be supported by both the Sustainable Transitions management team and your supervisory team. Additionally, all scholars can join the University of Essex’s ‘Centre for Environment and Society,’ which provides events and networking opportunities. Person Specification Only UK domiciled applicants who meet the following criteria may apply: Not already have a Masters’ degree. Be from a low-income household background as evidenced by, for example, being in receipt of a full maintenance loan or Special Support loan during their undergraduate studies. and/or Be one of the following categories of ethnicity: Black African Black Caribbean Black Other Mixed – White and Black Caribbean Mixed – White and Black African Other mixed background (including Black African, Black Caribbean and Black Other) Funding Details Home tuition fee waiver. Living costs stipend at the UK Research and Innovation recommended level per year. The stipend for 2026-27 is £21,805. A research allowance of £10,000 (in total) to be spent on authorised research costs, for example supplies and equipment, fieldwork etc. Closing Date: 11:59 pm BST on Monday 14th September 2026

item.description: The Department of Humanities and Social Sciences at the Mushtaq Ahmad Gurmani School of Humanities and Social Sciences (MGSHSS), Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position (Assistant Professor or above) in Political Science. About the Role We are seeking candidates with expertise in Quantitative Research Methods who can teach in this area alongside core Political Science courses. The successful candidate will contribute to the department's two undergraduate degrees — BSc (Honours) in Political Science and BSc (Honours) in Politics and Economics - both of which encourage students to explore Pakistan and the broader globalized world through diverse theoretical and methodological perspectives in the Social Sciences generally, and Political Science specifically. While candidates will primarily teach undergraduate courses (three per academic year), they will also have the opportunity to teach in the Department's newly launched M.Phil. in Society, Culture, and Politics (SCP). Candidate Profile Candidates should have a specialization in one or two of the following subfields: Comparative Politics International Relations Political Economy Applicants should demonstrate: A strong interest in and commitment to undergraduate teaching in Pakistan An active research and publishing agenda in one of the fields listed above A commitment to institution-building and to the intellectual life of the department and university Requirements Candidates must have completed their PhD or submitted their dissertation at the time of application. This is a full-time, on-campus position requiring physical presence for in-person teaching. How to Apply Interested applicants should submit: A current curriculum vitae A cover letter The names of three referees to hssrecruitment@lums.edu.pk Deadline: September 6, 2026 Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

item.title: Research Associate, El-Erian Institute for Behavioural Economics and Public Policy (Fixed Term)
item.description: Are you a passionate behavioural scientist eager to make a real-world impact? Do you want to conduct cutting-edge research at one of the world's most celebrated universities? If so, this is an opportunity not to be missed. Cambridge Judge Business School is seeking a talented and motivated Research Associate to join the El-Erian Institute for Behavioural Economics and Public Policy. Situated at the heart of the Cambridge Cluster, Europe's most successful technology entrepreneurship hub, the Institute brings together world-class minds to explore the frontiers of behavioural science, economics, and public policy. Led by its inaugural Director, the El-Erian Professor of Behavioural Economics and Public Policy, the Institute is a vibrant, collaborative community of around ten core researchers, united by a shared ambition to generate knowledge that truly matters. In this role, you will be at the forefront of interdisciplinary research, contributing to the full research lifecycle, from study design and data collection through to analysis, interpretation, and publication in leading international journals. You will have the opportunity to shape your own research portfolio, engage with policymakers and external stakeholders, support the next generation of researchers, and contribute to funding applications that drive the Institute's ambitious agenda forward. This is not simply a research post, it is a platform from which to build a distinguished academic career. We are looking for someone who combines intellectual curiosity with rigorous analytical capability. You will hold a PhD in social psychology, behavioural economics, or a closely related discipline, and bring strong expertise in experimental and quantitative methods, including proficiency in Python and Bayesian analytical approaches. A track record of high-quality, impactful research publications that demonstrate a meaningful contribution to the field, experience of policy engagement, and the ability to collaborate across diverse teams will set you apart. Familiarity with AI and LLM-based research methods would be a welcome addition. This is a two-year fixed-term appointment, based at Trumpington Street, Cambridge, with hybrid working available. The role is full-time with a start date of 18 January 2027. Interviews are planned for week commencing 24 August 2026. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click the 'Apply' button above. Informal queries may be directed to hrsupport@jbs.cam.ac.uk Please quote reference NS50509 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

item.title: Research Fellow, Sustainability and Resilience (focus on Social Issues)
item.description: About IMD The International Institute for Management Development (IMD) has been pioneering leadership development for nearly 80 years. Founded by business for business, we are an independent university institute with Swiss roots and global reach. Operating from Lausanne with strategic hubs in Singapore, Shenzhen, and Cape Town, IMD works with 19,000+ executives from 120+ countries annually. Our 145,000+ alumni form a powerful global network. Consistently ranked among the world's top business schools, IMD bridges cutting-edge research with real-world application to help leaders solve problems, scale solutions, and drive impact. Real Learning for Real Impact. To reinforce our team, we are looking for a Research Fellow, Sustainability and Resilience (focus on social issues) The Job’s mission The research fellow will work for the Risk & Resilience Initiative. The initiative is led by Prof. Florian Hoos and based on strong collaborations with Prof. Sophie Bacq and Prof. Karl Schmedders as well as a network of researchers from around the world. The main goal of the initiative is to bring the sustainability conversation back to the boardroom thereby ensuring the resilience and long-term value creation of firms. Concretely, this means helping corporate boards and investors integrate scientific knowledge (e.g., planetary boundaries, IPCC reports) and social foundations (e.g. what is at the core of Doughnut Economics) into corporate governance, opportunity and risk management. The initiative leverages IMD’s strengths in applied and scientific research, innovative executive education learning format development, and global dissemination, all based on strong partnerships, to maximize impact and longevity of the initiative. The Research Fellow will contribute to the initiative through developing and conducting novel and relevant research that fulfils the goals of the initiative, and is publishable in top-tier academic journals and relevant for practitioner outlets such that it can generate an impact beyond academia, particularly towards board members and investors. Publication formats therefore include academic- and practitioner-oriented articles, literature reviews, reports, and case studies. The research fellow should also ensure the successful completion of the publication process, and contribute to translating research results into materials for IMD teaching offerings, engagement platforms, and events. Key deliverables The aim of the Research Fellow’s work is to generate and disseminate impactful outcomes for both academic and practitioner audiences: Develop a clear research strategy in line with the initiative and publish in FT50 journals whereby we see value in both FT50-practitioner-oriented journals such as Harvard Business Review, and the more research oriented journals. We also see value in high impact journals such as Nature Sustainability or comparable journals. Distill key insights from the conducted research and publish white papers, cases, and other publication formats that reach a broader audience. Leverage various dissemination channels to communicate and translate the research insights into short communication formats. Engage stakeholders and gain partners for the initiative that support the research, and help disseminating the produced knowledge. Foster engagement with scholars across the globe for future impactful research dedicated to the objective of the initiative. Contribute to strategy development for the initiative that guarantees its long-term success Ideal profile Academic background: PhD in management, sociology, political science, economics, sustainable finance or a related field, with a clear focus on social impact aspects of sustainability for business, and ideally the interaction of social and environmental dimensions. The quality of the PhD should be proven through high quality working papers, or ideally through RRs or publications in top-tier academic journals such as FT50 journals. Substantive expertise: Evidence of research or fieldwork in one or more of the following areas is essential: Social impact measurement, Sustainability reporting, Sustainability strategy, human rights, dough not economics or further sustainability topics that focus on the social dimensions of sustainability and that are relevant to top managers and boards. Knowledge of sustainability reporting standards (CSRD, ISSB, GRI etc.) and frameworks is a plus. Methods: Strong qualitative (interviews, process tracing, case study design) and/or quantitative skills (econometrics, panel/archival data, field experiments, text analytics). Mixed‑methods experience is a plus. Output orientation: Demonstrated capacity to publish in top-tier academic journals and ideally also in practitioner outlets and other high outreach formats. Professionalism: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, ideally proven in interactions with high- level audiences (managers, politicians, executive education settings) Stakeholder engagement: Comfort engaging top managers and board members with different backgrounds and from different cultures. Attitude: Ability to work independently and proactively with minimum supervision. Collaborative and capable of working in a multi-disciplinary environment. Deadline and results oriented Language: Full fluency in English (written and spoken) is a must. Proficiency in French and/or German is helpful but not a requirement. Research Fellow Location: Lausanne, Switzerland or remotely Salary: Depending on experience and location Hours: Full Time (40 hours) or Part Time (minimum 20 hours) Contract Type: 3 years, Fixed-Term Closes: 06.09.2026 Start Date: ASAP How to apply If you have the above skills and would like to work in our stimulating environment, please send your complete application file (letter of motivation and resume in English, copies of your work certificates and diplomas) before September 6th 2026 via the above ' Apply ' button. If you’re a qualified candidate with a disability (such as dyslexia, sight and/or hearing disabilities, etc) and you need a reasonable accommodation in order to apply for this position, please specify it in your application. A valid Swiss work permit or Swiss or EU-25EFTA citizenship is required for this position.

item.title: Tenure-Track Associate Professor / Assistant Professor in International Relations
item.description: Applications are invited for appointment as Tenure-Track Associate Professor / Assistant Professor in International Relations in the Department of Politics and Public Administration (Ref: 536865), to commence in August 2027 or at another mutually agreed time, on a three-year fixed-term basis, with the possibility of renewal and consideration for tenure before the expiry of a second three-year fixed-term contract, both subject to satisfactory performance. Exceptionally outstanding candidates at the Associate Professor level may be considered for appointment on direct tenure terms subject to the University's approval. The Department of Politics and Public Administration is an internationally oriented research-focused department that covers a broad range of fields in Political Science and Public Administration. The Department offers three highly successful taught postgraduate programmes - Master in International and Public Affairs (MIPA), Master of Public Administration (MPA) and Doctor of Public Administration (DPA) - as well as a thriving undergraduate programme. More information about the Department can be found at https://ppa.hku.hk/ . Applicants should hold a Ph.D. degree by the time of appointment and demonstrate excellence in research and teaching. The Department welcomes applications from excellent candidates who specialise in any field of International Relations and is eager to both consolidate its existing strengths and to diversify into new areas of research and teaching. A highly competitive salary commensurate with qualifications and experience will be offered, in addition to annual leave and medical benefits. At the current rates, salaries tax does not exceed 15% of the gross income. The appointment will attract a contract-end gratuity and University contribution to a retirement benefits scheme, totalling up to 15% of the basic salary. Housing benefits will be provided as applicable. The University only accepts online applications for the above post. Applicants should apply online at the University’s careers site (via the above ' Apply ' button) and upload (1) an up-to-date CV, (2) a letter of interest, (3) graduate transcripts where relevant, (4) a research statement, (5) a teaching statement, (6) teaching evaluations where available, and (7) the contact information of three referees. Please also arrange for your referees’ letters of support to be sent directly to us at ppahr@hku.hk. We would be glad to receive these letters from Interfolio, your department administration or the referees themselves. Review of applications will begin on October 1, 2026. Further inquiries may be made to the Head of Department, Professor Robert Thomson, rthomson@hku.hk . The University is an equal opportunities employer and is committed to equality, ethics, inclusivity, diversity and transparency.

item.title: Local party organiser
item.description: As Local Party Organiser, you will support the Liberal Democrats across Ely and East Cambridgeshire so that: membership and the volunteer base grow; fundraising capacity increases to support local campaigning, including by the MP; we are better placed to fight elections, with campaigning and communications well coordinated; more Liberal Democrats are elected to the new unitary authority; we increase our majority at the next Parliamentary election. Priorities will be set by the local executive and campaign strategy team, with regional staff. Key responsibilities Support the campaign committee in strategic planning and organisation. Recruit, train, manage and motivate volunteers, and lead teams across doorstep, phone, online and delivery activity. Plan and deliver a sustained programme of doorstep and telephone voter contact. Oversee and contribute to campaign literature, and build our digital campaigning capacity. Manage campaign data and organise volunteers to do the same, in line with data protection rules. Liaise with the regional party, neighbouring local parties and council groups. Support the fundraising group as duties allow. Carry out other duties your line manager may reasonably require. You will also observe health and safety rules, uphold professional standards, promote equal opportunities and diversity, and take part in relevant training. Person specification Essential A strong self-starter, able to work unsupervised, manage your own workload, prioritise and meet deadlines. A can-do attitude and resilience under pressure. The ability to communicate effectively, in writing and in person, with a wide variety of people. The ability to motivate, manage and delegate to a team, and to work well within one. A willingness to learn new skills, software and ways of working. Sympathy with the aims and values of the Liberal Democrats. Desirable Knowledge of the local area and its politics. The ability to produce effective political literature. Experience of managing volunteers and running election campaigns. Good digital skills, including experience of, or willingness to learn, Connect, Lighthouse and Affinity Publisher. An eye for issues with campaigning potential, and confidence with local media. A full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle. Closing Date : 14 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Application Details Send you full CV of no more than two pages, including your full employment history and a contact telephone number and email address; and a covering letter of no more than two sides of A4, setting out why you want the role and how your skills and experience are relevant to it. Please also provide details of two referees, including at least one who can speak to your campaigning or relevant work experience. If you would prefer us not to contact your referees until a later stage, please let us know. Send your application to stephen.lambert@libdems.org.uk Website : https://www.libdems.org.uk/

item.title: Policy & Public Affairs Manager
item.description: Epilepsy Society is a dynamic charity with ambitious plans to revolutionise the lives of people through advocacy, research and care. We are looking for someone to join our award-winning campaigns team and help us to progress change through political engagement at both national and local level. We have an impressive track record of working with government, locally elected politicians, professional organisations, patient stakeholder groups and other charities in the sector on a range of issues which affect people with epilepsy. Our recent work includes our successful Zach’s Law campaign. This role is an exciting opportunity to help bring about further change that will make a real difference to the lives of people with epilepsy. The postholder will develop an effective programme of policy and public affairs work across the UK to have maximum impact for people with epilepsy and to raise the public profile of epilepsy. We seek someone with a degree or relevant experience in political or public affairs, extensive experience of influencing, organising campaigns and major events and negotiating at a senior level. You will be required to have a detailed level of understanding of government politics and the charity sector and an empathy to the cause. If you are interested in this role, please visit the link attached to this advert to view the full job description and to apply. Closing Date : 17 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Application Details https://app.vacancy-filler.co.uk/salescrm/Careers/CareersPage.aspx?e=LMo8nnTwYNZFZL2vkf3OYxEnvpmPQbtd0xAnM_O6g-DR3k5HxFqjhMDovXiw664AoiYcuFe3hdk Website : http://epilepsysociety.org.uk

item.title: Policy and Public Affairs Adviser
item.description: About the Role As Policy and Public Affairs Adviser, you will support the Electoral Commission's policy and public affairs work in Wales. This externally focused role sits at the heart of policy, legislation and democratic engagement. Working with Welsh Government officials, Members of the Senedd, political stakeholders and colleagues across the Commission, you will help shape the organisation's response to developments affecting elections and democracy in Wales. Key responsibilities include: Researching and analysing political, policy and legislative developments. Supporting engagement with Welsh Government consultations and legislation. Drafting consultation responses, briefings and policy papers. Building and maintaining stakeholder relationships. Supporting events and public affairs activity. Preparing advice for colleagues and supporting post-election reporting. About the Team You'll join a supportive team leading the Commission's work in Wales. The team works across policy, public affairs, electoral administration, regulation and stakeholder engagement, helping ensure the Commission remains a trusted voice on democratic issues. Who We're Looking For We're seeking a politically aware individual with strong analytical, communication and relationship-building skills. You'll be able to demonstrate: Experience in policy, public affairs or stakeholder engagement. Strong research and analytical skills. Ability to communicate complex information clearly. Experience building effective stakeholder relationships. Strong influencing skills and sound political judgement. Experience drafting reports, briefings or policy papers. Excellent communication skills and attention to detail. Welsh language skills are desirable. Why Work for Us? This is an opportunity to work on issues that matter to democracy in Wales, develop specialist expertise and engage with senior decision-makers. Benefits include: flexible and hybrid working, 28 days' annual leave rising to 30 days plus bank holidays, Civil Service Pension Scheme (28.97% employer contribution), study support, learning and development opportunities, Ride2Work and eye care vouchers. Closing Date : 17 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Week commencing 24 August 2026 in person at our Cardiff office. We encourage applications from disabled candidates and will seek to prioritise interviews for those meeting the essential criteria. Reasonable adjustments are available throughout the recruitment process and employment. Application Details How to Apply To support fair and inclusive recruitment, we use an anonymous recruitment process. Please submit an anonymised CV that does not include your name, address, contact details, date of birth, age, gender, ethnicity, nationality, photograph, or educational dates. Primary education details are not required. Please include your employment history, dates of employment, explanations for any gaps, and details of your duties, responsibilities and achievements. Applications containing personal details cannot be considered, so please check both your CV and file name before submitting. https://ce1002li.webitrent.com/ce1002li_webrecruitment/wrd/run/ETREC179GF.open?WVID=933737003x Website : https://www.electoralcommission.org.uk/

item.title: Local party organiser
item.description: Join the St Neots and Mid Cambridgeshire Liberal Democrats at a pivotal moment. Local government reorganisation will replace the county and district councils with new unitary authorities, so a major round of elections is coming, followed by the next General Election. This role puts you at the heart of those campaigns. You do not need to have done this before. You will receive full training and work alongside experienced campaigners, councillors and our MP. What matters is that you are motivated, well organised and get on with what needs doing. About the role You will grow our membership, volunteer base and fundraising, and help lead the campaigning that elects Liberal Democrats to the new unitary authority and increases our majority at the next General Election. Priorities are set by the local executive and campaign strategy team. Key responsibilities Support the campaign committee in planning and organisation. Recruit, train and lead volunteer teams across doorstep, phone, online and delivery activity. Plan and deliver a sustained programme of voter contact. Oversee and contribute to campaign literature, and build our digital campaigning capacity. Manage campaign data, and volunteers who handle it, in line with data protection rules. Liaise with the regional party, neighbouring local parties and councillors. Carry out other duties your line manager may reasonably require. You will also uphold professional standards and promote equality and diversity. Person specification Essential A self-starter, able to work unsupervised, prioritise and meet deadlines. Resilience under pressure. Confident communication, in writing and in person. The ability to motivate and manage a team. Sympathy with the aims and values of the Liberal Democrats. The ability to travel independently across the constituency. Desirable Knowledge of the local area, its politics and communities. Experience of managing volunteers, running election campaigns and producing political literature. Good digital skills, or a willingness to learn Connect, Lighthouse and Affinity Publisher. Workplace Your week will be flexible, split between home working and campaigning across the constituency. Some evening and weekend work is required. Closing Date : 14 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Application Details Send you full CV of no more than two pages, including your full employment history and a contact telephone number and email address; and a covering letter of no more than two sides of A4, setting out why you want the role and how your skills and experience are relevant to it. Please also provide details of two referees, including at least one who can speak to your campaigning or relevant work experience. If you would prefer us not to contact your referees until a later stage, please let us know. Send your application to stephen.lambert@libdems.org.uk Website : https://www.libdems.org.uk/

item.title: Caseworker
item.description: Rebecca Paul MP is seeking a Caseworker to join her team and support her in addressing constituents’ concerns on a wide variety of issues, such as SEND, healthcare, immigration, housing and benefits. You will be part of a small, driven and energetic team that is characterised by enthusiasm, self-motivation and adaptability. Key responsibilities: • Assess correspondence from constituents to identify how issues might be addressed • Draft responses to constituents and letters to agencies and ministers • Log all cases, monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken • Manage a large caseload, ensuring that each case is dealt with promptly, professionally, sensitively and accurately • Ensure cases and records are organised and information managed confidentially and in line with data protection legislation • Liaise with Government agencies, voluntary sector and others to resolve constituency matters • Assist the MP and other members of the team with additional tasks as required Essential skills and experience: • Excellent written and verbal communication skills – these may be tested at interview • Strong organisational abilities with attention to detail • Ability to work both independently and as part of a small team • Empathetic approach with strong interpersonal skills • Good knowledge of IT systems such as MS Office • Commitment to getting the best outcomes for constituents • Sympathetic to the aims and values of the Conservative Party Desirable skills • Previous casework or relevant experience • Knowledge of immigration, health, housing, social care or SEND • Familiarity with local constituency issues in Reigate • Full Driving Licence. Part-time applications may be considered. Additional information: Some work outside normal office hours will be required. Occasional travel within the constituency or to London may be necessary. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 14 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will take place on a rolling basis. We may appoint before the closing date so early application is encouraged. Application Details Interested candidates should send a CV and covering letter outlining their suitability for the role by 5pm on the closing date to sam.white@parliament.uk with the subject line ‘Caseworker Application’. Website : https://www.rebeccapaul.uk

The ideal candidate will be organised, reliable and have excellent attention to detail with superb customer service skills. item.title: Full-Time Caseworker
item.description: Contract: Full time (37.5 hours p/w) Elsie is looking for a full-time caseworker to work in her busy constituency office. The successful applicant will be happy to work both independently and as part of Elsie’s small, close-knit team. The role will be full-time and will allow for hybrid working both in the constituency office in Heywood, and remotely. Duties include: - Manage a large number of standard queries and more complex cases from members of the public. - Answering the telephone to constituents and handling incoming voicemails, and other correspondence. - Gather relevant information to assist with resolving cases. - Log all cases, monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken. - Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially in line with GDPR. - Draft high-quality responses to constituents. - Identify key themes emerging from casework and communicate these to the MP to raise in Parliament. - Ensure that each case is dealt with promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately, in accordance with the MPs requirements. - Assist at surgeries and other meetings and follow up as appropriate. - Develop and maintain systems that ensure proactive communication with constituents - for example, street letters. - Support with the organisation of constituency events and wider constituency engagement. - There will be a requirement to occasionally work outside of normal working hours, including attending events with the MP as required. Essential Criteria: - Previous experience working as a caseworker in a similar, public-facing role. - Ability to deal with and prioritise a large and varied workload and work well under pressure. - Ability to manage expectations in sometimes challenging circumstances. - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills. - Good IT skills including MS Office. - Ability to draft letters and emails to a high professional standard. - Motivation to work proactively and independently, as well as part of a small team. - Commitment to the aims and values of the Labour Party The role will focus on casework related to housing so knowledge and experience of housing casework would be desirable. Elsie welcomes applications from everyone regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, faith, disability or background. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 14 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed on Friday 21st August in Heywood. Ideally the candidate should be able to start on Monday 7th September, or very soon after. Application Details To apply please send your CV and 1 side A4 cover letter to: elsie.blundell.mp@parliament.uk by 12 noon on the closing date. You will only be contacted if you are successfully short-listed. Website : http://www.elsieblundell.org.uk Additional Notes August 4: removed 'pro-rata' from salary field

item.title: Graduate Consultant
item.description: The insights to advise and the relationships to deliver are built from the moment you enter the workplace. That’s why Lowick Hedry is launching Graduate Kick Start. Graduate Kick Start takes a graduate and turns them into an adviser who can work across all four of our practices – built environment, infrastructure, litigation & crisis, and public affairs – in twelve months. This isn’t a shadowing scheme. From week one you’re doing real, billable work for real clients, with the support in place to make sure you’re never out of your depth and the stretch to make sure you’re never coasting. You’ll also learn to use AI properly from the very start, through our in-house Vanguard programme. How you’ll be supported: A Personal Development Plan. Lowick Hedry Academy. A buddy for the day-to-day. Quarterly reviews against a competency framework spanning all four practices. What we’re looking for: A creative thinker and a clear writer. A real interest in politics, policy, and social issues. Experience making a difference in the world around us. Ownership and initiative whether in work, studies, or extracurricular. Complete the programme and you move into a permanent Consultant role, on a path to running your own accounts. Closing Date : 12 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Start Date: Autumn 2026 Application Details Please submit your CV and cover letter via our website by 6pm on the closing date. item.title: Two Research Officer/PhD Posts
item.description: The University of Tübingen is one of Europe’s oldest universities and in recent years has been very successful in the German federal and state governments’ Excellence Initiative. The Research Unit Comparative Public Policy at the Institute of Political Science of the University of Tübingen invites applications for Two Research Officer/PhD Posts (German public sector pay scheme TV-L E13, 75%) for the duration of 3 years from 1 November 2026 (or as soon as possible thereafter). Gross annual salary is commensurate with experience starting from approximately 43,000 Euro. The successful candidates will contribute to the externally funded research project “Measuring the Past and Assessing Future Possibilities of Welfare State Dualization” (DFG, German Research Foundation). Essential requirements: Excellent undergraduate and graduate degree in political science, sociology, or social policy Interest in and knowledge of comparative welfare state research and/or attitudinal research Excellent communication, presentation and writing skills in English (additional German, Swedish, Polish, and/or Italian language skills are beneficial) Excellent skills in qualitative and quantitative methods Excellent intercultural communication skills Ability to work both independently and as part of a team Disabled persons will be preferred in case of equal qualification. The University seeks to raise the number of women in research and teaching and therefore encourages qualified women academics to apply for these positions. If you are interested in this position, please send your application with the usual documentation (letter of motivation, curriculum vitae, copies of certificates, publication list or writing sample, etc.) in electronic form (one PDF file only) to: jakub.sowula@uni-tuebingen.de via the above 'Apply' button. Deadline for applications is 24.08.2026 (noon CEST) . Interviews are scheduled for 22 September 2026. For further questions, please contact: jakub.sowula@uni-tuebingen.de or martin.seeleib-kaiser@uni-tuebingen.de

item.title: Post-doctoral Research Fellow Level 2 - Temporary Fixed Term up to March 2030 (Part-Time 0.6FTE)
item.description: Applications are invited for a temporary part-time (0.6FTE) post of a UCD Post-doctoral Research Fellow Level 2 within UCD School of Politics and International Relations. The School of Politics and International Relations at University College Dublin invites applications for a Senior Postdoctoral Research Fellow Level 2 position on the Horizon Europe-funded project QUEST: The European Union's Quest for a Relational Open Strategic Autonomy. The successful candidate will contribute primarily to Work Package 10 (Defence Policy and Procurement) and associated cross-project activities examining the European Union's pursuit of Open Strategic Autonomy (OSA) in the fields of defence industrial policy, defence procurement and security governance. The postholder will undertake original research on EU defence policy instruments, defence-industrial cooperation, procurement frameworks, and the evolving relationship between strategic autonomy, economic security and European defence integration. Working under the supervision of the Principal Investigator, the researcher will contribute to comparative case studies, stakeholder engagement, academic publications, policy outputs and consortium-wide analytical activities. Closing date: 12:00 noon (local Irish time) on 18 th August 2026. Applications must be submitted by the closing date and time specified. Any applications which are still in progress at the closing time of 12:00 noon (Local Irish Time) on the specified closing date will be cancelled automatically by the system. UCD are unable to accept late applications. UCD do not require assistance from Recruitment Agencies. Any CVs submitted by Recruitment Agencies will be returned. The PD2 post is intended for researchers who have completed PD1. As with the PD1, if you have already completed your PD2 stage in UCD or will soon complete a PD2, or your total Postdoctoral experience, inclusive of the duration of the advertised post, would exceed 6 years, you should not apply and should refer to Research Fellow posts instead. Prior to application, further information (including application procedure) should be obtained from the Work at UCD website: www.ucd.ie/workatucd/jobs

item.title: Administrative Officer
item.description: Noah Law MP is looking for a skilled Administrative Officer to join his team. The successful candidate will support Noah’s constituency and Parliamentary work across St Austell and Newquay, through the triage and action of emails, telephone calls and social media enquiries, handling general enquiries, taking actions and minutes of meetings, and ensuring overall administrative efficiency in the office. This will include management of some casework in support of Casework staff, at times managing a small caseload of their own, and joining the MP in attending events or visiting constituents. They will also take responsibility for the administration and organisation of events and security apparatus as required, and keep track of invoices and receipts. The role will be based either in the constituency office or London office, following negotiation upon successful offer of the role. The successful candidate will report directly to the Office Manager, with other delegating of some tasks from the Parliamentary Assistant and Noah. The successful candidate will be highly organised, proactive, and dedicated to supporting a busy MP in a fast-paced environment. They will have a commitment to the Labour Party and its aims and values, and shall also be knowledgeable of Noah’s areas of interest. The role also involves general office duties such as answering calls, coordinating with external agencies, and drafting complex correspondence. The successful candidate should be able to handle enquiries efficiently, prioritise competing demands, and take initiative within a busy office setting. While the focus shall be administrative duties, the successful applicant will support other duties where required. There may be a requirement to work outside of the normal working hours and travel for visits occasionally, including supporting with constituency surgeries. This role is a full time role (40 hours per week) until March 31st, 2027, in the first instance. Extensions to the contract will be subject to other factors. item.title: Policy and Communications Officer

item.title: PhD Studentship - Narratives of Enslavement and their Legacies
item.description: Start date: February 2027 King’s College London’s Leverhulme Centre for Research on Slavery in War is pleased to announce the availability of a fully funded AHRC doctoral studentship from October 2026, to be jointly supervised across the English and War Studies departments by Dr. Michael Collins(English) and Dr. Maeve Ryan (War Studies). We invite proposals under the theme of: “Narratives of Enslavement and their Legacies” Project scope and research questions Applicants are invited to propose innovative research exploring any element of the relationship between narratives of slavery broadly defined (including post-enslavement life-writing and the “slave narrative” genre; the legacies of enslavement in fiction and the transatlantic literary traditions; and critical theories of race and racialisation emerging from histories of enslavement and indenture) written in English between the period of 1776 and the mid twentieth century. Due to the specialisms of the proposed supervisors, focus on the British Empire and the U.S. is preferred, but modes of transnational engagement and comparativist readings across national and linguistic traditions are highly encouraged. Since the candidate will be situated across two faculties, The Department of English and the Department of War Studies, an interest in questions of how geopolitical conflict, conflict-based diasporic movement, and the conditions of war have affected and shaped narrative traditions would be an advantage. The LCRSW is driven by a singular, transformative vision: to learn from the past in order fundamentally to change how the world understands, forecasts, and tackles the enduring problem of slavery in war. How, where and why has slavery in war emerged over time? How has slavery influenced the course, conduct, and consequences of war? How have slavery and war shaped the evolution of legal and normative frameworks throughout history? What are the needs of survivors of slavery in conflict? Consequently, potential methodological and conceptual areas of interest for proposals may include (but are not limited to) readings of narratives of enslavement through theories of: Racial Capitalism (Robinson) Narratology Environmental Humanities/ The Plantationcene (McKittrick) Ontologies and “Genres” of the Human (Wynter) Transnationalism Human Rights and Legal Frameworks British Studies, American Studies, Settler Colonial Studies, Multicultural Studies It is expected that the candidate will have strong skills in use of archives (identifying and defining their archival focus will be a major element of the first year of the doctorate) and a willingness to engage in forms of public outreach work appropriate to their research, in conjunction with the ‘Leverhulme Centre for Research on Slavery in War' and The Department of English. The studentship can be taken up either full or part-time. Students should have an excellent academic record. A master’s degree in a relevant subject (such as Literature, History, American Studies, War Studies, Development Studies, Anthropology, Cultural Studies) is a requirement. If you are unsure about the appropriateness of your disciplinary training, please reach out to either potential supervisor to discuss the proposal in advance. Details of award The award pays UKRI Home Tuition Fees (£5,238 for 2026/27) for PhD students. The award pays full maintenance for all students both home and international. The UKRI Doctoral Stipend for 2026/2027 is £21,805, plus a London Weighting of £2,000/year, plus Collaborative Activity funding at a rate of £600/year. Further details can be found on the UKRI website: www.ukri.org/manage-your award/studentship-guidance/support-for-ukri-funded-students The student is eligible to receive an additional Research Training Support Grant (RTSG) during the course of the project The project can be undertaken on a full-time or part-time basis. Eligibility This studentship is open to both Home and International applicants. However, the CRSW is limited to one Overseas studentship across the opportunities currently advertised. We are committed to welcoming applications from students from all backgrounds. We particularly welcome applications from Black, Asian, minority ethnic (BAME) backgrounds as they are currently underrepresented at this level in this discipline. We require an upper-second class (2:1) honours degree and a Master’s degree at high merit or above in a discipline directly relevant to the PhD (or international equivalent). Please see here for the English-language requirements for PhD students in the Department of War Studies (Band B): Postgraduate English language entry requirements | King's College London Assessment of applicants Applicants will be assessed by how well they meet the person specification for this position. This may include: An educational and research background that matches this research project. The potential to work effectively and inclusively with a diverse team of people The potential to take initiative and manage a dynamic and complex workload. The potential to develop expertise in new areas related to this subject. A demonstrated interest in and understanding of the proposed area of research, including knowledge of current challenges and opportunities. The potential to undertake continuous personal and professional development. The potential to communicate ideas and findings, verbally and in writing, clearly and effectively. An understanding of relevant research methods. How to apply If you have questions about the project or the application process, please contact Kelsey Carthew at crsw@kcl.ac.uk Applicants should apply at the link below and submit the following no later than 5pm on 1 st September 2026: qualtrics.kcl.ac.uk/jfe/form/SV_0UQML35ytEOvOHc Curriculum vitae A personal statement outlining your reasons for pursuing doctoral research at King’s College London A research proposal (5-10 pages in length) that explains your proposed area of focus; primary research question; importance and originality of your topic; initial thoughts on methods and potential case studies; and your familiarity with the existing literature and research on this topic. A sample of academic writing. If you are a current MA student awaiting results of your dissertation, please upload your submitted dissertation as your writing sample. Transcripts of undergraduate and master’s qualifications One academic reference Please submit all materials in English. Use of AI: While we recognise that AI tools can be useful for certain tasks, your application should reflect your own thinking, research interests, skills, and experience rather than AI generated content. Applications that rely heavily on AI-generated content may not demonstrate the originality, critical thinking, and personal insight expected for doctoral study. Please note it is the responsibility of applicants to request references from their referees and ensure that they have been received by this deadline. All documents should be submitted in either MS Word or PDF format. Interviews will be held in September with offers expected by the end of the month. Following the interview, the successful candidate will also need to formally apply to King’s College London and satisfy its admission requirements.

item.title: PhD Studentship - Slavery and the Seven Years’ War within and across the Caribbean Archipelago
item.description: Start date: February 2027 King’s College London’s Leverhulme Centre for Research on Slavery in War is pleased to announce the availability of a fully funded AHRC doctoral studentship from October 2026, to be jointly supervised across the History and War Studies departments. We invite proposals under the theme of: “Slavery and the Seven Years’ War within and across the Caribbean Archipelago” Project Scope and Research Questions This doctoral project will explore the relationships between military conflict and slavery in the context of the Seven Years’ War (1756-1763), often characterised as the first global war. The Seven Years’ War has generally been understood as a top-down military conflict between European powers, played out on a global stage. Displacing this traditional understanding of centre and periphery, this thesis will trace participation in the war from the ground up by individuals, networks, companies and colonial operators across notional imperial divides. The primary research object is to resituate slavery as both a core constituent and production of military conflict. While slavery has figured in important accounts of the Seven Years War, particularly for the contemporaneous occurrence of important ‘slave revolts’ such as Tacky’s War (1760-61), this thesis will be the first to conceptualise the relationship between slavery and war at the heart of this global conflict. Within this broad area of inquiry, applicants may propose their own area of focus, primary research questions, conceptual frameworks, methodological approaches and case studies. Projects with a transnational and multilingual focus are encouraged. Some important questions or topics this thesis might explore include: 1. Enslaved labour in the military: the official and unofficial presence of enslaved people dispatched by Caribbean plantation owners as island deployments and contributions to colonial military forces. 2. The impact of the Seven Years’ War on trafficking and trade with West Africa (including on the internal politics of precolonial West Africa) 3. The experiences of enslaved people, whose lives were shaped and influenced by military conflict. Thinking through survival, military experience and the conditions of war can reshape records of enslaved lives, more often understood as ‘freedom narratives’ and ‘fugitive archives’. 4. Abolitionism and the reinterpretation of slavery as a political, legal, and moral conundrum in the context of war. The thesis will use records across company and colonial archives: the East India Company and the Royal African Company, as well as papers in the National Archives Colonial Office Series, the Prize Papers, and the records of the High Court of Admiralty. As a critical historical case study in the deeper (re)conceptualisation of slavery and war at the heart of the Leverhulme Centre for Slavery in War, this project will have important implications for longer durée histories of slavery, colonialism, and empire. The candidate recruited to this role will be supported to participate in this collaborative research programme. They will be expected to contribute research to central datasets, and will be encouraged and supported to develop high-profile publications at the cutting edge, interdisciplinary nexus of archival research, applied history, and social science. The studentship can be taken up either full or part-time. Students should have an excellent academic record. A master’s degree in a relevant subject (such as History or War Studies) is a requirement. About the Leverhulme Centre for Slavery in War Nearly 90% of recent armed conflicts have involved some form of slavery. Yet the relationships between slavery and war are little examined and poorly understood, leaving governments, international institutions, and humanitarian actors ill-prepared to prevent, respond, or address deep, long-lasting impacts. In a world facing proliferating conflicts, the Leverhulme Centre for Research on Slavery in War (LCRSW) is the first overarching and integrative academic initiative dedicated to understanding the complex, pervasive, and persistent slavery-war nexus as it has evolved over the centuries. This dual-site research centre (led by the Department of War Studies at King’s College London and the Rights Lab at the University of Nottingham) has been established to shape a new interdisciplinary field of study and a step-change towards the global goal of eliminating forced labour, modern slavery, and human trafficking. The Centre’s research agenda is structured around four interconnected Research Strands (RS): (Re)conceptualising (RS1), Understanding (RS2), Forecasting (RS3), and Tackling (RS4) slavery in war. Doctoral research projects will be embedded within and across these research strands and their teams, working both individually and as a cohort. Together, they will break down disciplinary silos, integrating methodologies from across the AHRC subject remit—primarily history, literature, law, digital humanities, human geography, philosophy, classics, gender studies, political science, and international studies—with cutting-edge data science techniques, including Earth Observation (EO) data analysis, machine learning, large-scale collation and analysis of survivor narratives, geospatial analysis, future-crafting approaches, and novel simulations known as ‘peace- gaming’. Students will also have opportunities to collaborate with our institutions’ partners around the world, across the policy, practitioner and academic sectors. Details of award The award pays UKRI Home Tuition Fees (£5,238 for 2026/27) for PhD students. The award pays full maintenance for all students both home and international. The UKRI Doctoral Stipend for 2026/2027 is £21,805, plus a London Weighting of £2,000/year, plus Collaborative Activity funding at a rate of £600/year. Further details can be found on the UKRI website: www.ukri.org/manage-your award/studentship-guidance/support-for-ukri-funded-students The student is eligible to receive an additional Research Training Support Grant (RTSG) during the course of the project. The project can be undertaken on a full-time or part-time basis. Eligibility This studentship is open to both Home and International applicants. However, the CRSW is limited to one Overseas studentship across the opportunities currently advertised. To be classed as a home student, candidates must meet the following criteria: We are committed to welcoming applications from students from all backgrounds. We particularly welcome applications from Black, Asian, minority ethnic (BAME) backgrounds as they are currently underrepresented at this level in this discipline. We require an upper-second class (2:1) honours degree and a Master’s degree at high merit or above in a discipline directly relevant to the PhD (or international equivalent). Please see here for the English-language requirements for PhD students in the Department of War Studies (Band B): Postgraduate English language entry requirements | King's College London Assessment of applicants Applicants will be assessed by how well they meet the person specification for this position. This may include: An educational and research background that matches this research project. The potential to work effectively and inclusively with a diverse team of people The potential to take initiative and manage a dynamic and complex workload. The potential to develop expertise in new areas related to this subject. A demonstrated interest in and understanding of the proposed area of research, including knowledge of current challenges and opportunities. The potential to undertake continuous personal and professional development. The potential to communicate ideas and findings, verbally and in writing, clearly and effectively. An understanding of relevant research methods. A successful proposal will contain a clearly identified, novel research question, positioned in the context of current historiography. It will also identify relevant sources. Compelling proposals will offer insight into how the candidate may use those sources. How to apply If you have questions about the project or the application process, please contact Kelsey Carthew at crsw@kcl.ac.uk Applicants should apply at the link below and submit the following no later than 5pm on 1 st September 2026: qualtrics.kcl.ac.uk/jfe/form/SV_0UQML35ytEOvOHc Curriculum vitae A personal statement outlining your reasons for pursuing doctoral research at King’s College London A research proposal (5-10 pages in length) that explains your proposed area of focus; primary research question; importance and originality of your topic; initial thoughts on methods and potential case studies; and your familiarity with the existing literature and research on this topic. item.title: Assistant Professor in International Relations/International Political Economy
item.description: LSE is committed to building a diverse, equitable and truly inclusive university As an equal opportunities employer strongly committed to equity, diversity and inclusion, we encourage applications from women and people from ethnic minority backgrounds as they are currently under-represented at this level in this area. All appointments will be made on merit or skill and experience relative to the role. Department of International Relations Assistant Professor in International Relations / International Political Economy Salary is no less than £68,087 per annum and the salary scale can be found on the LSE website Based in the Department of International Relations, the post holder will contribute to the intellectual life of the School through conducting and publishing outstanding quality research, engaging in high quality teaching as instructed by the Head of Department, and participating in the Department and wider School activities. All candidates must have expertise and research interests in International Relations or International Political Economy, with a specialism in Global Environmental Politics, Environmental Justice or Energy Politics. They must show a clear, well-developed and viable strategy for future outstanding research that has the potential to result in world-leading publications. The successful candidate must be able to teach undergraduate and postgraduate courses on International Relations, or International Political Economy, and Global Environmental Politics, Global Ecology, Energy Politics. Candidates will need a completed PhD, or be close to obtaining a PhD, in International Relations, Political Science, or a related field by the post start date. Candidates should also have a proven ability, as evidenced by existing publications, or potential to publish in top refereed international journals, or with highly respected book publishers, in the field of international relations. Successful candidates should have excellent communication skills and an ability to work as part of a team with colleagues across the School. item.title: Research Officer (Comparative Politics)
item.description: Location: Queen Elizabeth House, 3 Mansfield Road, Oxford OX1 3TB The Oxford Department of International Development (ODID) is seeking to recruit a Research Officer. Reporting to Professor Masooda Bano, the post-holder will join a research team funded by a European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant, Choosing Islamic Conservatism: Muslim Youth in Europe and the UK and the Question of Social Cohesion. Building on the earlier phases of the project, the team is now establishing the European Muslim Observatory: Comparative Research Infrastructure on Muslim Institutional Development in Europe. The Observatory aims to develop the first systematic comparative research infrastructure documenting the institutional development of Islam and Muslim communities across Europe. It will bring together legal, political, institutional and religious data to examine how Muslim institutions evolve in interaction with constitutional frameworks, state institutions and wider society, creating a lasting research resource for comparative scholarship on Islam in Europe. The Observatory aims to establish a lasting comparative database that will support future academic research, policy engagement and international collaboration beyond the lifetime of the current ERC grant. Successful applicants will become part of the founding research team responsible for designing, developing and implementing this new research infrastructure. This post is offered full-time for 18 months. The successful candidate will have a Master's degree (or equivalent) in Comparative Politics, Political Science, European Studies or a closely related discipline. They will also possess excellent analytical and organisational skills. The ability to work systematically with large volumes of information is essential to this role. At ODID we embrace and cherish our differences, and endeavour to be considerate and welcoming of all. You are most welcome at ODID, without the need to hide any part of who you are. We acknowledge societal inequalities and how these affect us, and those around us, personally and professionally. We hold an Athena Swan bronze award in recognition of our efforts to introduce organisational and cultural changes which promote equality, cherish diversity and create a better working environment for all. We are also taking active steps to promote race equality and reduce the risk of bias and discrimination. We work together to enrich, fortify and grow our community and dedicate our combined efforts to teaching and research to increase our impact and influence in development debates at the national and global level. We encourage all eligible candidates to apply for our vacancies and join us in pursuing our goals. Applications for this vacancy are to be made online. You will be required to upload a CV and supporting statement as part of your online application. Please note that only the CV and supporting statement will be considered; any other documents uploaded will not be reviewed as part of the shortlisting process. Only applications received before 12 midday on Friday, 11 September 2026 can be considered. Contact Person: HR Team Pay Scale: RESEARCH GRADE 6 Contact Email : recruitment@qeh.ox.ac.uk
