item.title: PhD Student with Strong Computational Profile for the Project Navigating Negativity: What is a Healthy News Diet?
item.description: The Centre for Journalism, Department of Political Science and Public Management , University of Southern Denmark, Odense, invites applications with a strong computational profile for a three-year full-time PhD scholarship in the project Navigating Negativity: What is a Healthy News Diet? (HEALTHY NEWS), with employment starting from 1 November 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter. The place of employment will be in Odense. The research project—funded by the Velux Foundation—examines when exposure to negative news informs people about important societal issues and when it negatively affects mental well-being and leads to news avoidance. The overall aim is to identify barriers and opportunities for healthy news diets and to assess how the benefits and drawbacks of negative news can be balanced in today’s individualized media environment. Motivated applications are invited from candidates holding a master’s degree in relevant fields, such as computational social science, computer science, communication, political science, or journalism/media studies. The PhD student will be involved in all aspects of the research, from conception, execution, analysis, publishing to public dissemination. The ideal candidate therefore has a high academic level and a good grasp of research designs and methods. Strong computational skills are necessary. The application deadline is 15 September 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST) For more information, please click on the ' Apply ' button above.

item.description: About the role As a Senior Electoral Practice and Performance Adviser, you will play a key role in supporting the effective delivery of elections and electoral registration services across Wales. Working closely with Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), Returning Officers (ROs), local authorities and other electoral stakeholders. Key responsibilities include: Providing professional advice and guidance on electoral law, policy and practice to electoral administrators across Wales. Delivering and supporting the Commission's performance standards framework for Returning Officers and Electoral Registration Officers. Analysing electoral performance information, identifying trends, risks and opportunities for improvement. Building strong relationships with local authorities, the Electoral Management Board for Wales and other key stakeholders. Developing guidance, resources and reports that support the delivery of high-quality electoral services. Leading specific projects and workstreams while managing your own portfolio of work. The ability to manage projects, workstreams and competing priorities effectively. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. The confidence to influence, negotiate and work collaboratively with a range of stakeholders. High levels of integrity, impartiality and commitment to public service Welsh language skills are desirable in this role would be advantageous but is not essential. You’ll need excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to convey complex information clearly and concisely. You’ll deal with a wide range of social and policy casework. item.description: Overview of techUK’s Health & Social Care Programme: With health and care systems around the globe facing increasing pressures, the use of digital technology has never been more important. techUK’s Health & Social Care Programme supports the digital health and care supplier community, representing our members to the public sector and fostering a vibrant ecosystem. techUK helps members navigate the complex space of digital health and care in the UK and ensure our NHS and care services are prepared for the challenges of the future. Role Purpose: The purpose of this role is to support techUK’s Health & Social Care Programme team, as well as developing key workstreams independently. This position provides an opportunity to work with senior level representatives from across the health, social care and life sciences sectors, to support the delivery of policy and market engagement opportunities for our members. This role would suit an articulate and enthusiastic learner, with the ability to support the development of new policy and the delivery of projects and events. The role will encompass the development the programme’s work in health, social care and life sciences, exploring the role of digital health and technology in improving these sectors. Experience organising events, analysing policy, or working with one or more of the following is desirable: the UK technology sector, NHS, government, or policy makers. The successful candidate will demonstrate the capability to work across multiple workstreams, engaging with a variety of industry and government stakeholders, and will develop a good understanding of the opportunities and challenges facing the health technology sector. Key Responsibilities: Support the development, implementation and communication of techUK activities to deliver value for member companies; Support the development, implementation and management of the programme’s work across the health and social care sectors, developing expertise in key areas; Support with the set-up and execution of in-person and virtual events, briefings and meetings; Promote techUK activities through written insights, social media engagement and PR/media activities; Support the team to bring new companies into techUK membership. item.title: Campaigns Manager - Eastbourne constituency
item.description: Eastbourne Liberal Democrats are seeking an ambitious, organised and hands-on Campaigns Manager to lead campaigning in one of the party’s strongest constituencies. Following Josh Babarinde OBE’s election as MP in 2024 and major Liberal Democrat gains in the 2026 East Sussex County Council elections, this is an exciting opportunity to help deliver winning campaigns at a pivotal moment. Elections to a new East Sussex unitary authority are expected in May 2027, with further elections likely over the following years. Working closely with the MP, councillors, candidates, local party officers and campaign teams, you will develop a constituency-wide electoral strategy and turn it into day-to-day delivery. Responsibilities include campaign planning; voter contact; messaging, literature and targeting; volunteer recruitment and development; fundraising; candidate support; data analysis; training; and supplier management. We need someone who can think strategically while remaining practical and delivery-focused. You will be highly organised and self-motivated, able to manage competing priorities, build strong relationships and inspire volunteers. You should have experience of delivering complex campaigns, projects or workstreams; excellent communication skills; sound judgement; confident IT and digital skills; and sympathy with the aims and values of the Liberal Democrats. Experience of political campaigning, working with elected representatives or volunteer-led organisations, delivering training, and using Connect, Lighthouse or Affinity Publisher would be an advantage. A full driving licence and access to a vehicle are also desirable. The role reports to the South East Regional Campaign Manager and offers scope for professional growth and increased responsibility. Applicants must be eligible to work in the UK. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and will make reasonable adjustments during recruitment. For the full job description and to apply, visit: https://bit.ly/EBcampaignmanager Closing Date : 16 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews: Friday, 21st August 2026 Application Details Please submit an application form here to apply: https://bit.ly/EBcampaignmanager Job Description and Person Specification: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1N7oacP8mZPw8tkwXebka4ITwKBbBn8C_/edit Website : https://www.eastbournelibdems.org.uk/

Leading on the management of a wide and fast evolving range of constituency campaigns and work streams Lead on designing effective media and communication campaigns in support of his Westminster - Managing or supporting the management of all aspects of the offices Parliamentary budget There may be requirement for the role holder to work outside of the normal working hours, including attending events with the MP as required Essential skills and experience: Excellent written and verbal communications skills and exceptional attention to detail. The Digital Engagement Officer will lead on writing copy for our digital comms, focusing on our member and supporter mailings, website and social media, and manage our mailing list and inboxes. We’re looking for someone with experience of managing mailing lists and writing copy for a variety of audiences and actions. You should have experience crafting digital communications that motivate people to take action, and be excited about creating journeys over time that integrate the threads of our fundraising, national campaigns, local organising and ideas output together into the story of Compass. You should have a background in digital engagement, specifically in direct marketing through mailings or copywriting for fundraising and campaigning, ideally with a familiarity with CRM software and GDPR regulations. You should have a keen understanding of the political landscape in which Compass operates and be interested in progressive political ideas and working in a pluralist way to make change happen. Writing and editing with various actions in mind, including event invitations, fundraising asks and campaigns. Proofreading mailings, publications, funding bids. Maintaining and updating our CRM records including donor information. Managing our inboxes to connect to supporters and steward our members. As the principal link between the Parliamentary Group and external organisations, the successful candidate will develop productive, trusted relationships with elected representatives, parliamentary officials, journalists, business leaders, public bodies, charities, community organisations, policy groups and opinion formers. Working closely with the Chief of Staff, Deputy Chief of Staff, MSPs and colleagues across the Policy Resource Unit and Communications Team, you will provide high-quality strategic advice, political intelligence and stakeholder insight to support parliamentary activity, policy development, media work and campaign priorities. Operating in a high-profile and fast-moving political environment, you will exercise excellent judgement, discretion and professionalism while representing Reform UK Scotland at senior external levels. Key Responsibilities • Develop and implement Reform UK Scotland's external affairs strategy. • Build and maintain relationships with parliamentarians, public bodies, businesses, trade associations, charities, think tanks and community organisations. • Lead stakeholder engagement programmes across Scotland. • Monitor parliamentary business, committee activity and legislative developments. • Coordinate parliamentary engagement and stakeholder meetings. • Provide strategic political intelligence and advice to senior leadership. • Identify opportunities to influence public policy and political debate. • Develop stakeholder engagement plans aligned to parliamentary priorities. • Organise policy forums, roundtables, conferences and stakeholder events. • Represent Reform UK Scotland at meetings, events and external engagements. • Prepare high-quality briefing papers, reports and speaking notes. • Build positive relationships with journalists and media organisations. • Support reputation management and responses to politically sensitive issues. • Produce political intelligence reports and stakeholder analysis. • Lead external affairs workstreams and contribute to organisational planning. item.title: Membership and Communications Coordinator
item.description: The Association for Citizenship Teaching (ACT) is the national subject association for Citizenship education. We support teachers, schools and education leaders through professional development, curriculum resources, research and policy engagement, helping ensure every young person receives a high-quality Citizenship education. This is an exciting time to join ACT. Following the Government's Curriculum and Assessment Review, Citizenship education is being strengthened across secondary education and introduced as a statutory subject in primary schools for the first time. ACT is working closely with government, parliamentarians and education partners to help shape the future of the subject. We are looking for a Membership and Communications Coordinator to join our small, friendly and collaborative team. The role combines membership administration, customer service and digital communications. You will be the first point of contact for many of our members while supporting the delivery of communications across email, website and social media. Key responsibilities include: Providing excellent membership administration and customer service. Maintaining and developing our CRM database and membership records. Supporting email marketing and member communications. Drafting and publishing website and social media content. Supporting marketing campaigns and membership growth. Providing administrative support across communications, events and organisational projects. Monitoring membership and engagement data to inform decision making. We're looking for someone with excellent organisational and communication skills, experience of administration or customer service, strong attention to detail and an interest in communications, marketing and education. As a small national charity, every member of our team makes a meaningful contribution. This is an excellent opportunity to develop a broad range of skills while working alongside teachers, policymakers and education organisations to strengthen Citizenship education across England. Closing Date : 1 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews are expected to take place shortly after the closing date. We will contact shortlisted candidates with further details once applications have been reviewed. item.title: Social Organising Lead
item.description: As Social Organising Lead, you will lead 411's social organising function - leading strategy, methodology, and delivery of programmes that help clients grow their movements and turn supporters into online activists. You'll oversee a team of specialists, delivering campaigns that are creative, scalable, and grounded in real-world organising principles. The role involves building clients' internal organising capacity - training teams, developing supporter journeys, and designing systems that sustain mobilisation, working closely with client teams and Strategic Directors. Specific Responsibilities Strategy: Develop and lead strategies for clients, including supporter journeys and mobilisation frameworks. Team Leadership: Lead and mentor a team of specialists, fostering excellence and collaboration. Line manage junior staff. Ensuring high level of delivery: Oversee programmes, ensuring work is well-executed, politically astute, and results-driven. Organising Methodology: Develop methods for online mobilisation, from peer-to-peer outreach to volunteer management. Capacity Building: Design and deliver training that builds organising capability within client organisations. Experience 3+ years' experience in community organising, online mobilisation, or political campaigning. Experience managing a small to mid-sized team (line management a plus). Political, union, or third sector/NGO experience is desirable. Experience running social media campaigns. Skills Ability to translate organising strategy into clear, practical plans. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including training and inspiring others. Strong presentation skills. Confidence using AI tools to accelerate planning and scale organising work. Ability to prioritise workload in a fast-paced environment. Knowledge of another language is helpful but not essential. item.title: Campaigns Lead
item.description: This is a new role at ECU, being recruited as part of a wider programme of work to deepen the relationships between national organisations working on economic systems change and grassroots campaigners. The Campaigns Lead will work closely with the Head of Campaigns on driving forward our high-impact campaigns for economic systems change. For at least the first year, the Campaigns Lead will be working primarily on our coalition campaign on the cost of living crisis, Cost of Living Action. The campaign, which is currently made up of over 40 organisations from across civil society, unions and grassroots groups, aims to end the cost of living crisis and put in place solutions to prevent it from ever happening again. It focuses on our policy demands in five areas that drive the cost of living crisis: wages, social security, energy, housing and taxation. The campaign positions itself as the civil society coalition focused on the cost of living as a whole, and that solutions to it must be addressed that way. The campaign relaunched in early 2026 and has a vital role to play in putting media and political pressure on the government to take action. We also work closely with those most impacted by the crisis and aim to centre the voices of those with lived experience of economic hardship in all that we do. This role will shape and drive forward a programme of impactful communications, advocacy and other campaigning activities under the rebooted campaign to secure transformative changes that bring real improvement to people’s lives. There is ample opportunity to engage politically in this role, increasing as you develop in the position. The full description and job pack can be found here: https://www.econchange.org/recruitment/campaigns-lead Closing Date : 17 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates The closing time for applications is 9am Application Details Apply via Workable here: https://apply.workable.com/j/CC55514278 Website : http://www.econchange.org/

item.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
item.description: The Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies (PIIRS) at Princeton University is pleased to announce the call for applications to the PIIRS Postdoctoral Fellowship Program for the 2027-28 academic year. As a leading global institution in interdisciplinary research on international issues, PIIRS is dedicated to advancing innovative scholarship that addresses the world's most pressing challenges. The PIIRS Postdoctoral Fellows Program is integral to that mission. We will award up to four postdoctoral fellowships to our 2027-28 cohort. PIIRS seeks recent PhDs in the Social Sciences who have demonstrated exceptional scholarship, congruent with the Institute's intellectual focus, that simultaneously advances theoretical debates in their disciplinary field; creatively speaks to and engages with a multidisciplinary audience; and deepens substantive regional knowledge of specific places. Appointments will be made at the rank of Postdoctoral Research Associate and are for one year (12 months) with the possibility of renewal pending satisfactory performance and continued funding. Postdoctoral Research Associates are expected to be in residence at Princeton or the local vicinity for the entire academic year or demonstrate to the program’s satisfaction the ability to be on campus on a daily basis and on short notice in order to fulfill responsibilities relating to in-person participation. The position requires Postdoctoral Research Associates to be on campus at least four days per week. Leveraging Princeton's scholarly resources, fellows will focus on research, expand their intellectual horizons, and prepare work for publication. They will have biweekly meetings with the faculty director to share their work, and monthly meetings with faculty fellows from various social sciences to present their work and learn from others. Fellows are also encouraged to engage with colleagues and attend departmental seminars. Applicants must demonstrate outstanding scholarly achievement and promise. To be eligible, applicants generally cannot have more than two years of postdoctoral experience prior to the start of the appointment, at the beginning of the academic year on September 1, 2027. The postdoctoral selection will be made based on the strength of the candidates' scholarly record; the promise of the proposed research; and the ability to contribute to the intellectual life of the postdoctoral program (with interest in connecting with other PIIRS and Princeton departments on campus). In addition to a competitive salary and benefits, the program will provide the Fellow with the opportunity to host a small, pre-publication, book workshop; and a research fund of $4,000 per year. The program will also provide shared office space, and a laptop computer. Further information can be found at here . This position is subject to the University's background check policy. The work location for this position is in-person on campus at Princeton University. Position is not eligible for sponsorship of an H-1B visa requiring consular processing; other visa sponsorships (including H-1B visas not requiring consular processing) may be available, as appropriate. Application Instructions Applications are due by September 15, 2026 (11:59 p.m. EST). The following application items should be uploaded by the applicant: Cover letter Curriculum vitae Transcripts Research Proposal indicating plans for two-year postdoc (maximum 5 pages double-spaced) Dissertation abstract (including Table of Contents) Writing sample: one chapter of the dissertation or one published article related to dissertation topic. Document confirming either that you have completed all requirements for the PhD degree or a letter signed by your dissertation advisor indicating that you will complete the PhD by the start date of the fellowship. The names and email addresses of three referees, who will be contacted automatically by the online application system with an invitation to upload their letter of recommendation to the system by the application deadline. (**Please note: all letters of reference should be submitted by your referees before September 15, 2026. deadline. **) Equal Employment Opportunity Statement Princeton University is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

item.title: Account Manager
item.description: The Account Manager delivers public affairs, stakeholder engagement and communications consultancy across infrastructure projects. The role spans client and internal work, and involves close collaboration with the wider team and freelancers. The AM is a strong collaborator with an entrepreneurial spirit — proactive, willing to ask questions and raise ideas, with the tenacity to go beyond the brief. Drawing on consultancy and/or in-house experience, they identify compelling narratives and opportunities, and drive advocacy with political, business and other stakeholders. Duties & Responsibilities The Account Manager will: Demonstrate IM values and behaviours in all ways of working. Deliver impactful campaigns and high-quality materials to support client objectives. Manage relationships with senior project stakeholders and clients, and with a wide range of external stakeholders — business leaders, local and national government, special interest groups and local communities. Develop stakeholder mapping, manage stakeholder databases, produce briefing notes and identify potential advocates. Work with technical experts across client teams to translate complex information for varied audiences. Progress to leading client accounts and project-managing deliverables, team members, and hours/billing. Work with graphic designers and videographers on infographics, animations, video case studies, presentations, brochures and maps. Support the IM leadership team on corporate materials and projects. Assist in developing new business pitches and proposals. Monitor Government and Parliament activity relevant to clients and business development. Research new infrastructure projects and developments in planning policy. Take on other duties as needed to maintain a high standard of work. Person Specification Demonstrable interest in and knowledge of UK politics, including local, regional and devolved government, policy and infrastructure. High level of collaboration. Skilled communicator, written and spoken. Track record of building and managing relationships. Campaigning mindset. Enthusiastic and entrepreneurial. Comfortable with stakeholders at all levels, from junior staff to CEOs. Experience in a relevant field, with the ability to translate this into positive outcomes for the team. Closing Date : 20 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Early applications encouraged. We may appoint before the closing date. item.description: Gareth Davies MP is looking for a Parliamentary Assistant who is a proficient communicator to join his team. The person in this role will support him by raising awareness of, and contributing to, his Parliamentary activities. The successful candidate will be a self-starter, who enjoys producing creative, substantive and engaging content. They will also be able to exercise good political judgement, and use their own initiative to and problem-solving skills to both start and complete communications and research projects. The applicant should be highly motivated and expect to work to tight deadlines. Main responsibilities will include but are not limited to: • Publicising Gareth's activities as MP and related news. • Producing, updating and monitoring Gareth’s online content, including his website and social media. • Producing online graphics and video content. • Monitoring media coverage, liaising with the media, and preparing press releases as required. • Managing and monitoring social media queries and comments. • Undertaking research on relevant subjects as directed and assisting with casework as required. Capabilities required: • Very strong IT skills, with proficiency across various social media platforms, are essential. • Strong research, analytical and writing skills. • Ability to learn quickly and work under pressure. • Highly organised, able to prioritise and manage a heavy workload. • Personal initiative and a proactive work ethic. • Personable and able to work as part of a small team. • The ability to maintain complete discretion and confidentiality. Desired Experience/Qualities: • Experience in online content creation would be a strong advantage, including experience using graphic editing software such as Canva and video editing and producing software. • Experience in graphic and design skills, including photography and/or videography would be an advantage. • Understanding of the Grantham and Bourne constituency would be preferable. • Supportive of the aims and values of the Conservative Party. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . item.title: Communications Campaign Officer
item.description: The Home Office works to build a safe, fair and prosperous UK. We achieve this through our work on counter-terrorism, policing, crime, drugs policy, immigration and passports. The Corporate Services Group works closely with the Home Office’s policy and operational commands to enable us together to deliver the department’s priorities. The group is comprised of different teams and professional functions, including Commercial, Communications, Finance, People, Portfolio and Project Delivery, Private Office, Security, Estates and Information. As a member of the Communications Directorate, you’ll be supporting our mission to deliver outstanding public services that work for everyone. You will join a multi-disciplinary team with colleagues based across the UK, working together to deliver the Home Office’s communications strategy. We believe a positive, open and supportive culture is crucial to help everyone deliver their best work. We value diversity and provide an inclusive and encouraging environment for our team members. We nurture our talent and offer a broad range of learning and development opportunities to help you fulfil your potential. Successful applicants will be a highly motivated, adaptable, innovative, dependable and collaborative communications professional, prepared to work on some of the most challenging, high profile and interesting issues in government. You will support the planning, delivery and evaluation of communications campaigns aligned to major government priorities, such as securing the border, reducing illegal migration and tackling knife crime, to create measurable change among audiences. You will work with a multi-disciplinary team, including press, marketing, insight, internal communications, external affairs and social media specialists. And you will build and maintain positive relationships with internal and external stakeholders. You will be expected to manage content production and work with agencies where needed, while also having the opportunity to bring your own creative ideas to life. This will involve managing plans, ensuring activity remains on schedule and delivering value for money. item.description: The Royal British Legion is looking for a confident and politically aware Public Affairs and Campaigns Officer to lead impactful campaigning activity across the North of England, including North East, North West, and Yorkshire & the Humber regions of England. This is an opportunity to work at the heart of issues affecting the Armed Forces community, turning insight into action and ensuring the voices of veterans, serving personnel and their families are heard where it matters most. From influencing local decision-makers to shaping meaningful conversations across communities, you’ll play a visible role in driving positive change on behalf of those who have served. We’re looking for someone who understands how local government and public affairs really work; someone who can build credibility quickly, spot opportunities to influence and create campaigns that connect with people on a local level. You’ll be equally comfortable briefing MPs and councillors, working alongside community stakeholders, organising events and translating national priorities into campaigns that feel relevant and tangible within local communities. This role would suit someone who thrives on relationship-building, enjoys working across a varied political landscape and has the confidence to represent a nationally respected organisation in high-profile settings. In return, you’ll join a passionate and collaborative team working on issues that genuinely matter. No two days will look the same, and the impact of your work will be visible across the region. Whether you’re developing local campaign networks, supporting Armed Forces Covenant activity or helping influence policy conversations at a grassroots level, you’ll have the freedom to bring fresh thinking, new ideas and your own approach to engagement. If you’re motivated by purpose, skilled at influencing others and want to be part of an organisation committed to making a lasting difference to the Armed Forces community, we’d love to hear from you. item.description: Adam Dance MP, Member of Parliament for Yeovil, was elected as the Liberal Democrat MP for Yeovil in July 2024, and is looking for an enthusiastic, professional and organised person to join his team as a caseworker (20 hours). item.title: Member Governance Officer
item.description: We are looking for a highly organised, professional, and impartial Member Governance Officer to join our Member Governance Team based in our Leeds office. The Member Governance team is a small but effective team that sits within the wider Member Services Team and plays a crucial role in ensuring the resolution of disciplinary matters relating to Party members. Member Governance Officers are responsible for conducting investigations in accordance with the Party’s Code of Conduct and associated Rules. They make the initial assessments on if a complaint falls under the Code and then manage the progression of the case under the Party’s processes. The role includes the handling and processing of sensitive and sometimes protracted disciplinary matters which must be handled impartially, empathetically, and professionally. Member Governance Officers must offer support to other colleagues in the handling of disciplinary matters and complaints as well supporting with the work of the Disciplinary Sub-Committee of the Party Board as secretary to hearings. They are responsible for the bulk of the correspondence from the Member Governance Team with them handling dismissals and investigations as well as general correspondence through the complaints management system. They also provide support to the wider Member Services Team in the handling of day-to-day matters in busy periods or when covering annual leave. They work as the primary support to the Designated Safeguarding Lead on safeguarding matters and administration. item.title: Jewish Health Equity Partnership – Programme Director, Project Lead
item.description: Job 1- Programme Director Full time - 5 years Funding Period Salary £48,000-£50,000 Purpose of the role To lead delivery of the Jewish Health Equity Partnership, delivering systems partnerships within the Jewish community, influencing policy and practice across the health sector, and ensuring successful delivery of the programme’s workstreams in collaboration with partners. The Programme Director will lead JHEP’s operational relationships with partners across the Jewish community and the health sector, building relationships to bring about structural change. The postholder will bring experience of project delivery and stakeholder management within the health sector. This would ideally include familiarity with NHS, ICS, health trusts, public health, commissioning, workforce and/or health equity settings, together with a strong understanding of how antisemitism and structural discrimination affect Jewish communities and wider health outcomes. Job 2- Project Lead Part time / 5 year funding period. Salary £30,000 pa (£75,000 FTE) To provide senior strategic leadership and oversight for the programme, ensuring strong governance, high-quality delivery and effective alignment between strategy, partnerships, evidence and impact. The Project Lead will act as a senior ambassador for the programme, supporting external credibility, funder confidence and long-term sustainability. This role sits at the intersection of health inequalities, structural racism, antisemitism and systems change. The postholder will bring senior-level experience of the health sector, ideally including NHS, Integrated Care Systems, public health, commissioning, workforce or health equity settings, together with a strong understanding of how antisemitism and structural discrimination affect Jewish communities and wider health outcomes. This is an opportunity to establish and lead a pioneering national programme that will shape how Jewish health inequalities are understood and addressed across England. item.title: Partnership Director
item.description: About Spacehive Spacehive is the crowdfunding platform for ideas that bring local places to life, from turning phone boxes into community libraries to pop-up gardens, street art and neighbourhood markets. Over £45 million has been raised on our platform, and we have the highest success rate of any UK crowdfunding platform. We work with an ambitious network of funding partners (councils, combined authorities, government bodies and brands across the UK and Ireland) who back locally-led projects that matter to their communities. About this role As Partnership Director you'll lead our client portfolio and set the direction of our award-winning community crowdfunding partnerships. You'll drive strategic planning, own relationships and manage contracts. We've deliberately rebuilt this role around an AI-powered operations hub, so programme tracking and reporting run on automated workflows and the team spends its energy on what actually moves partnerships forward. You'll have a Partnership Manager reporting to you, plus close support from Business Development, Projects and Finance. What you'll own The client portfolio and its revenue: retention, renewals and growth The strategic direction of each partnership: programme strategy, fund mapping, senior stakeholder engagement A modern, AI-enabled way of working, helping shape the tools as they evolve A high-performing team, line managing and developing a Partnership Manager New client onboarding and growth, alongside Business Development Our impact story, presenting to senior stakeholders and leading client events About you An experienced account leader in partnerships, account management or client services, with commercial instincts (Local Authority experience a bonus) A confident communicator who manages senior stakeholders with differing priorities Systematic and organised, keeping multiple programmes on track A strategic thinker with an eye for growth Genuinely curious about AI and comfortable directing automated output Spacehive is an anti-racist, anti-discriminatory organisation. We particularly welcome applications from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic people, people with disabilities, and people from lower income and diverse educational backgrounds who may be under-represented in our organisation. item.title: Research and Policy Officer
item.description: Reports to: Research Manager Location: London / Hybrid (two days a week in office – EC1V 0JR) Hours: Full time (35 hours a week) Contract: 2-year fixed term contract (extension subject to funding) Salary: £37,213 NJC SCP 22 (band 22–27 inc. London Weighting) Annual leave: 25 days increasing by one day per year up to a maximum of 30 days (+ 2 additional days + birthday leave + office closure between Christmas and New Year, in addition to public bank holidays). Other benefits: 7% employer pension contribution, cycle to work scheme, annual wellbeing budget and employee wellbeing assistance programme. Introduction The Prison Reform Trust (PRT) was founded in 1981 to inform and influence public debate on prison conditions and the treatment of prisoners, amidst concerns about a projected prison population of 48,000 by 1984. With the prison population in England and Wales projected to rise to as high as 114,800 by March 2028, the charity remains as important to civic society today as it was then. Our mission is clear: we are working to create a just, humane and effective prison system by influencing decision makers, opinion formers and the public to 1) reduce the use of prison; 2) improve treatment and conditions for prisoners; and 3) promote equality and human rights in the justice system. Job purpose The Research and Policy Officer is a new blended role that reflects the close relationship between PRT’s research and policy functions. The successful candidate will play a crucial role in supporting both activities by helping to deliver research projects that drive policy and legislative change, as well as contributing directly to policy activities through evidence reviews and consultation submissions (functionally line managed by the policy and communications manager). The role will also involve assisting with delivery of the PRT’s flagship publication the Bromley Briefings Prison Factfile. You will have a solid foundation in quantitative and qualitative research methods and some experience of using them in applied research, together with an excellent understanding of the penal system in the UK and the associated research literature. If this sounds like you, you will be joining a reputable organisation with exceptional leadership, extensive networks and a proven track record of promoting evidence-based policy to achieve reform. Key responsibilities Research Collect, process and manage quantitative and qualitative data from primary research projects. This will periodically involve countrywide travel for prison visits, sometimes overnight. Carry out quantitative and qualitative analysis in accordance with agreed research designs and analytical frameworks. Support the compilation, management, cleaning and analysis of complex datasets from official sources. Assist with the transcription, coding and synthesis of qualitative material. Undertake literature reviews and rapid evidence syntheses drawing on academic, policy and practitioner sources. Follow established research workflows and quality-assurance processes to ensure outputs are accurate and reliable, including the Bromley Briefings Prison Factfile. Support the maintenance of research databases, documentation and project records. Assist with the production of research reports, briefings and presentations. Contribute to the communication and dissemination of research findings to policymakers, practitioners and the public. Support wider research function tasks, including coordinating meetings, stakeholder engagement and general administration. Policy Contribute to consultation responses, parliamentary briefings and other policy-related outputs. Conduct desk research and literature reviews to inform policy work Assist the Policy and Communications Manager in delivering policy activities. General responsibilities Participate in team meetings and contribute to organisational planning. Represent PRT externally where appropriate. Undertake administrative tasks necessary for the effective functioning of the Policy, Communications and Research team. Carry out any other duties commensurate with the responsibilities of the post. How to apply Please send your CV, cover letter (2 sides A4 maximum) addressing how you meet the above criteria and completed recruitment monitoring form via the 'Apply' button above (e alex.guthrie@prisonreformtrust.org.uk) by 5pm on Monday 24 th August. We must receive all 3 documents to process your application, and we will request any documents not received. Your recruitment monitoring form will be processed separately from your application. If you would like an informal chat about the role please contact our research manager Sophie Ellis, sophie@prisonreformtrust.org.uk . Interviews will be on Monday 21 st September at our offices at 15 Northburgh Street, London EC1V 0JR . Thank you for your interest in working for the Prison Reform Trust. For more information and to download the monitoring form please visit our website: www.prisonreformtrust.org.uk/opportunities

item.title: Senior Caseworker
item.description: Claire Hazelgrove MP is looking for a committed and organised Senior Caseworker to join her constituency office. The Senior Caseworker will support Claire to be an active, impactful and approachable MP. You will lead the casework function and work with a Caseworker to provide advice and support to local people on a range of issues. Managing a large caseload, organising MP advice surgeries, and supporting relevant events, you will help resolve problems for local people through communication with government agencies, local authorities, the voluntary sector and other organisations. Holding a senior role in the team, and working with others, you will collate and surface trends which can inform wider policy change efforts of the MP and team. Key Responsibilities: Lead and oversee the casework and wider direct resident support function of the team Deal with large numbers of standard queries, as well as leading on the more complex individual cases - by phone, email, or face to face - in a professional, confidential, caring and sensitive manner Ensure that each case is dealt with promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately in accordance with the MP Plan and organise MP advice surgeries, including identifying and booking residents in for appointments, arranging appropriate venues across the constituency Identify and surface trends and produce relevant reports on issues faced by residents, working across the team to support policy change and campaigning efforts led by others in the team on these, and reporting back to residents Support the Caseworker in their continued growth and development Work collaboratively across the team on relevant project work to help residents more easily access support and to highlight the impact of casework in supporting residents Required skills and values: Ability to deal with and prioritise a large and varied caseload, and work well under pressure Ability to manage expectations in sometimes challenging circumstances Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills Ability to work independently as well as effectively as part of a small team Ability and willingness to work outside of normal hours and travel for work occasionally Discretion and professionalism Sympathetic to the aims, values and objectives of the Labour Party Desirable skills Previous casework experience Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 23 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Closing time: 10pm Interviews: Thursday 10th September 2026 Start date: To be agreed, and based on notice period, but as soon as possible Application Details Please send a relevant CV and one page covering letter outlining how you meet the job specification and your interest in the role to: clairehazelgrovemp@gmail.com quoting ‘Senior Caseworker Application - Your First and Last Name’ in the subject line. Due to the high volume of expected applications we are only able to contact you if you have been shortlisted. Thank you. Website : http://clairehazelgrove.co.uk

item.title: Communication and Constituency Officer
item.description: Nesil Caliskan MP is looking to recruit a full-time, Communication and Constituency Officer to support her work for the constituents of Barking. The role will be based in the constituency to help promote her work locally through communications, as well as support tasks in the constituency office. Duties will include, but not limited to: Attend constituency meetings as appropriate Maintain a communications plan for the Member, planning for content across all channels and coordinating with the agreed priorities and campaigns of the Member Produce literature and social media content for constituency campaigns and to promote the Member at constituency activities such as, street stalls, coffee mornings, meetings with resident associations Establish, monitor and update a social media and online presence in the constituency. Produce online graphics and video content, as well as publicising surgeries and news alerts etc. Manage and monitor social media enquiries, dealing with cases that do not need to be transferred to a higher level. Ensure all enquiries are dealt with in a timely manner Monitor media coverage, liaise with media, prepare press releases as required (on constituency, non-party-political matters) Produce press releases, liaise with the media, meeting deadlines as appropriate Flexible working, including the occasional weekend, will be expected and TOIL can be accrued There may be a requirement for the role holder to work outside of the normal working hours and travel for work occasionally Candidates with previous communication experience is desirable, but not essential, however all candidates should have a good understanding of different social media platforms and how Members of Parliament can utilise them to engage with their constituents. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 28 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews: via Teams, week commencing 31st August. Start date: as soon as possible. Applications close at 5pm. Application Details CV and cover letter. Cover letter should be no longer than two sides of an A4 page. Send both to theo.antoniou@parliament.uk with the subject line: [YOUR NAME] - Communication and Constituency Officer application. Website : http://www.nesilcaliskan.com

item.title: Caseworker
item.description: This is an opportunity to help make a real difference to people's lives in Chelsea and Fulham. The caseworker will work alongside the established casework and policy teams and be expected to work collaboratively as well as independently. They’ll split the time dealing with both casework and policy enquiries from constituents. Experience in a similar role providing support to individuals will be considered. The position requires excellent communication skills; the ability to speak, write and listen well as well as strong administrative and organisational skills to manage a busy workload. Key Responsibilities Act as a first point of contact for constituents via telephone and email including handling high volumes of enquiries, engaging with a wide range of constituents over the phone, including those who may be distressed or dissatisfied, demonstrating patience, resilience, and professionalism. Supporting the MP in his work with constituents by providing support through liaison with government agencies, local authorities, the voluntary sector and others. Draft responses to constituents on casework and policy matters. Managing, progressing, and monitoring a heavy caseload. Maintaining an up-to-date knowledge of relevant guidelines/legislation. Ensuring cases are dealt with in a sensitive and confidential manner. Working effectively as part of a small team, showing initiative and taking ownership of your work. Person & Job specification Experience of carrying out casework preferred. Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Experience of dealing with challenging individuals in a calm, professional and respectful manner. A high standard of written English with attention to detail. Can prioritise work effectively and work independently. Has excellent administrative and organisational skills. Experience of dealing with sensitive and confidential information. Competent use of IT packages. A commitment to helping people and getting the best results possible for residents. A positive, approachable manner with the ability to contribute to a supportive and good-humoured team environment. Sympathetic to the aims and values of the Labour Party. Occasional evening work might be required. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 23 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates We aim to shortlist week beginning 24th August, and interviews will take place the following week. Please indicate your availability to start in your application. If invited to interview you will be required to complete a written exercise. Start Date – ASAP upon appointment. Application Details To apply, please send us a covering letter and CV with the subject line “ Caseworker Vacancy ” to ben.coleman.mp@parliament.uk . In your cover letter, please set out what you think the main issues in Chelsea and Fulham are likely to be in the next few years. Website : http://www.bencoleman.uk

item.title: Communications Officer
item.description: Wendy Chamberlain MP is looking for a highly motivated, professional individual to join her team as a Communications Officer. The role involves producing quality written content, whilst promoting parliamentary and constituency activities, and providing a range of communications support in a fast-paced Westminster environment. Wendy looks forward to hearing from you, if you thrive on making a difference, welcome the challenge of working in a busy political office and want to play an essential part in communicating her work. Key responsibilities • Prepare press releases, liaise with the media, meeting deadlines as appropriate. • Manage and monitor social media ensuring all enquiries are dealt with in a timely manner and escalating where required. • Maintaining and updating the MP’s E-newsletter and website. • Develop engaging and targeted content across a range of platforms. • Monitor media coverage and identify opportunities to promote the MPs work. • Build and maintain strong relationships with local, regional and national media outlets. • Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially in line with data protection legislation. • Support the MP in her Westminster role when required. • Support the MP’s priorities and communicate effectively with constituents of all demographics to reflect how her work supports concerns in North East Fife. Key Skills • Excellent written and verbal communication with the ability to engage confidently with a range of audiences and deliver key messages. • Excellent organisational skills and strong attention to detail. • The ability to work independently, and as part of a small team. • Manage competing tasks and respond quickly to the changing political environment. • Be able to engage effectively with a range of stakeholders both in Westminster and the Constituency. An understanding of UK parliamentary procedures, government policy, and current affairs is welcomed with an awareness of devolved issues which the MP may reference on behalf of constituents. Travel to the Constituency may be required and occasional work out with business hours. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 24 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Candidates will be contacted week commencing 31st August 2026 with an update and Interviews will be held early September 2026. The first Interview may be held virtually, and the second interview in person. The start date is as soon as possible. Ideally October 2026. Application Details Applicants should send a covering letter (no more than one page) and a CV (maximum two pages) to Arlene.Campbell@parliament.uk When submitting your content, please use the Header “Name – Communications Officer”. If you have any questions in advance of your submission, please email Arlene Campbell. Website : https://www.wendychamberlain.scot/

item.title: Assistant Professor of International Relations (Tenure-Track)
item.description: The Department of Political Science at Northwestern University seeks applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor in International Relations to begin on September 1, 2027. We seek candidates who will advance international relations scholarship and engage with important issues in contemporary world politics. The successful applicant will teach a combination of graduate and undergraduate courses. A Ph.D. in Political Science or a closely related field, with International Relations training, is required. ABD applicants who anticipate completion of the doctorate by Fall 2027 will be considered. Applicants must provide a curriculum vitae, cover letter, writing sample, research statement, teaching statement, and three letters of recommendation. Review of applications will begin immediately, and all applications received by September 15 will be given full consideration. To apply, click the 'Apply' button For inquiries about job advertisements or the application process, please contact Stephen Monteiro, Business Administrator in the Political Science Department. stephen.monteiro@northwestern.edu . Salary The expected base pay range for this position is $100,000 - $125,000. This base pay range is for a nine-month academic appointment, does not include summer salary, and is subject to negotiation. Northwestern University has provided a pay range representing its good faith estimate of what the university reasonably expects to pay for the position. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors including (but not limited to) the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate including years since terminal degree, training, and field or discipline; departmental budget availability; internal equity; and external market pay for comparable jobs. Benefits At Northwestern, we are proud to provide meaningful and competitive benefits. The available benefits package for this position will include health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance; paid medical/sick and parental leave; tuition benefits for the employee and dependents; pre-tax and flex spending accounts for commuting and dependent care; generous retirement savings options; and wellness programs. For a comprehensive overview of available benefits, including eligibility details, visit us at Northwestern Benefits to learn more. Northwestern University is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics, including disability and veteran status. View Northwestern’s non-discrimination statement . Job applicants who wish to request an accommodation in the application or hiring process should contact the Office of Civil Rights and Title IX Compliance. View additional information on the accommodations process .

item.title: Research Assistant/Associate - Postdoctoral Researcher in Modern Dravidian Studies (Fixed Term)
item.description: The Faculty of History wishes to recruit a Research Assistant/Research Associate within the broad field of 'Modern Dravidian History and Politics 1945-to the present, working under the supervision of Professor Shruti Kapila, Professor of History and Politics. The position is endowed by a recent bequest to the School of Humanities and Social Sciences. This is a full-time post for three years, commencing 1 October 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter. The pathways and aims of this research are to build historical and analytical perspectives on welfare in relation to shifts in democracy and statecraft including emerging digital public infrastructure. A combination of methods - archival, data sets and interview based will be essential. The interaction of ideas and institutions with public perception, political languages and democratic outcome will be key. The ideal candidate will be educated to PhD level, with established expertise in South Asian/Tamil history or politics (or clear evidence that completion of such a doctorate is imminent) and will have fluency with the use of research materials in English and Tamil; proven ability to conduct and deliver a high quality research project; be an experienced Microsoft office user, prepared to learn other software tools if required and have the ability and willingness to engage in digital humanities research and public -facing work, in a collaborative and inter-disciplinary capacity. The postholder will undertake innovative research with data sets, archives and interviews on welfare, democracy and postcolonial statecraft and other repositories utilising Tamil language. With the supervision of Professor Shruti Kapila, they will: Write research articles where appropriate from their own work and move towards publishing a monograph at the completion of their postdoctoral fellowship. Work with Prof Kapila on to identify key sources for digital humanities research and to design and manage the public platform for the project as required. Work closely and collaboratively with colleagues including doctoral students and postdoctoral fellows; and further afield, academics, public intellectuals and others. Fully participate in workshops and conferences connected to the project by presenting papers and assisting with arrangements; attend other conferences, held by other associations and groups, when possible. Work with and inter-disciplinary research and writing with a view to presenting ideas and policy perspectives to stakeholders, public and scholarly audiences. Engage with tasks connected to the dissemination activities of the project. More information about the Faculty is available here: https://www.hist.cam.ac.uk/ Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available until 30 September 2029 in the first instance. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click the 'Apply' button above. Informal enquiries are welcomed and should be directed to: Professor Shruti Kapila ( sk555@cam.ac.uk ) If you have any queries regarding the application process, please contact: hr@hist.cam.ac.uk Please quote reference JJ50616 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.
